summary: Failed/successful execve paths clear fs_struct::in_exec outside the intended cred_guard_mutex window while clone(CLONE_FS) observes the flag.

call_chain.evidence: sets fs->in_exec while holding fs->lock and cred_guard_mutex
ground truth names copy_fs as the clone(CLONE_FS) reader; fs/exec.c comments name copy_fs protection

bug_site.code: reads fs->in_exec under fs->lock when deciding CLONE_FS sharing

interleaving: Exec sets fs->in_exec=1 during unsafe-exec checks.
If exec fails or succeeds, the old code cleared current->fs->in_exec later without the same cred_guard_mutex ordering.
A sibling clone(CLONE_FS) path can observe or overwrite the flag, so the fix moves clearing into begin_new_exec()/free_bprm() while cred_guard_mutex is held.

access_b.code: copy_fs reads fs->in_exec to reject CLONE_FS during exec

ground_truth_access.required_ordering: The in_exec flag must be cleared while still protected by cred_guard_mutex so concurrent exec/clone users cannot observe a stale or prematurely cleared state.

vulnerability_surface.why_relevant: The boolean state flag gates clone(CLONE_FS) sharing during exec and is the exact field reordered by the patch.

aliases.name: p->fs->in_exec
aliases.evidence: sets the flag after checking fs users

aliases.name: current->fs->in_exec
aliases.evidence: old clear site after exec success/failure

thread_a.evidence: exec path owns the current fs_struct

thread_b.evidence: CLONE_FS attempts to share the same fs_struct

allocated_by: fs_struct allocation for task filesystem state

coverage.analysis_conclusion: fs/exec.c contains the patch, the writer, and the comments documenting copy_fs protection. copy_fs is noted as an external stack/candidate file because the existing focused bitcode covers the patched behavior but not kernel/fork.c.

patch_hunks: Clears current->fs->in_exec in begin_new_exec() and free_bprm(); removes later clears in bprm_execve().
indirect_edges: exec_binprm() calls begin_new_exec() through binfmt handlers.
entry_discovery_log: exec.ll contains bprm_execve, check_unsafe_exec, begin_new_exec, and free_bprm.
notes: copy_fs is not present in the focused case source/bitcode; the two-context model is still supported by the commit message and fs/exec.c comments.
